body.statement: Using \(H_{\mathrm{WF}}\), establish or refute universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, without a dominance restriction, \[c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}\le\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le C\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\},\qquad C^{-1}\omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)\le C\omega_\alpha(w,q).\] The proof must certify the explicit capped optimizer and its trimming dual, including all-measurable externally randomized intervals. When no cap binds, it must give \(\omega_\alpha=\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\).
body.justification: Outside the Lindeberg regime, the explicit finite program makes the dominance-aware claim falsifiable rather than naming an unspecified modulus.
body.gap: BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 gives graph-subset MSE bounds; neither derives an exact confidence-dependent weighted-clique water-filling program.
body.consumer: The optimizer identifies blocks that remain quadratic, hit their outcome cap, or should be protected by trimming.
